headline: 51 dead as floods and landslides hit 7 districts in Bangladesh
summary: Over 1 million people affected as heavy rains and flash floods devastate southeastern and northeastern regions.
details: According to the Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief, 51 people have been killed and 39 others injured due to floods and landslides caused by heavy rainfall and hilly torrents.
Cox's Bazar has been the hardest hit, recording 28 deaths, including 13 Rohingya refugees. One person remains missing in the district.
Other fatalities include 13 deaths in Chattogram, 6 in Bandarban, 3 in Rangamati, and 1 in Moulvibazar.
Currently, 58 upazilas across Khagrachhari, Rangamati, Bandarban, Cox's Bazar, Chattogram, Moulvibazar, and Habiganj are submerged under floodwaters.
More than 267,000 families have been stranded, affecting over 1.022 million people in total.
The government has opened 1,131 shelters, providing refuge to over 44,000 people.
To support the victims, the government has allocated approximately 9,000 metric tons of rice and 46 million BDT across the seven affected districts and the rest of the country.
caption:
51 people dead and over 1 million affected. Bangladesh's floods and landslides have left a trail of devastation.

According to the Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief, 51 people have been killed and 39 others injured due to floods and landslides caused by heavy rainfall and hilly torrents.

Cox's Bazar has been the hardest hit, recording 28 deaths, including 13 Rohingya refugees. One person remains missing in the district.

Other fatalities include 13 deaths in Chattogram, 6 in Bandarban, 3 in Rangamati, and 1 in Moulvibazar.

Currently, 58 upazilas across Khagrachhari, Rangamati, Bandarban, Cox's Bazar, Chattogram, Moulvibazar, and Habiganj are submerged under floodwaters.

More than 267,000 families have been stranded, affecting over 1.022 million people in total.

The government has opened 1,131 shelters, providing refuge to over 44,000 people.

To support the victims, the government has allocated approximately 9,000 metric tons of rice and 46 million BDT across the seven affected districts and the rest of the country.

headline: Iran renews attacks on US Gulf allies after 7th night of US strikes
summary: Iran has targeted US military bases in Kuwait and Bahrain and desalination plants, escalating the conflict after a ceasefire collapsed.
details: Iran launched renewed attacks on US Gulf allies today, following a seventh consecutive night of US strikes targeting Iranian military sites and logistics infrastructure.

In Kuwait, Iran's Revolutionary Guards struck a US military support centre at Camp Arifjan and a radar facility at Ali Al Salem Air Base. A desalination plant was also hit, and operations at Kuwait International Airport were suspended due to missile and drone threats.
In Bahrain, the Revolutionary Guards targeted an intelligence data centre and a site where US combat aircraft were gathered at Sheikh Isa Air Base.
The US military's Central Command reported concluding its seventh day of strikes by hitting Iranian surveillance sites, underground weapons storage, and maritime capabilities.

Civilian infrastructure has been increasingly targeted. In Iran's Hormozgan Province, three people were killed and eight wounded in strikes that damaged bridges and a tunnel. In Jask, 10,000 people were left without water after missiles hit desalination pumps.
Oil prices climbed more than 4% to their highest level in over a month, as both sides targeted shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for one-fifth of the world's oil supply.
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres expressed concern over the escalation and the attacks on civilian infrastructure across the region.
US President Donald Trump has threatened broad-based air strikes on Iran's infrastructure and has not ruled out a ground assault on Iran's coast or islands.
caption:
Iran has launched renewed attacks on US Gulf allies, hitting military bases in Kuwait and Bahrain and critical water plants.

Iran launched renewed attacks on US Gulf allies today, following a seventh consecutive night of US strikes targeting Iranian military sites and logistics infrastructure.

In Kuwait, Iran's Revolutionary Guards struck a US military support centre at Camp Arifjan and a radar facility at Ali Al Salem Air Base. A desalination plant was also hit, and operations at Kuwait International Airport were suspended due to missile and drone threats.

In Bahrain, the Revolutionary Guards targeted an intelligence data centre and a site where US combat aircraft were gathered at Sheikh Isa Air Base.

The US military's Central Command reported concluding its seventh day of strikes by hitting Iranian surveillance sites, underground weapons storage, and maritime capabilities.

Civilian infrastructure has been increasingly targeted. In Iran's Hormozgan Province, three people were killed and eight wounded in strikes that damaged bridges and a tunnel. In Jask, 10,000 people were left without water after missiles hit desalination pumps.

Oil prices climbed more than 4% to their highest level in over a month, as both sides targeted shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for one-fifth of the world's oil supply.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres expressed concern over the escalation and the attacks on civilian infrastructure across the region.

US President Donald Trump has threatened broad-based air strikes on Iran's infrastructure and has not ruled out a ground assault on Iran's coast or islands.
